title: Race tests that pass without their lock
when: Clinic gates G02-02 to G10-23, early November 2026
source: Clinic slice S04 session a9b52f2e; check-summary.md line 75; task.md line 303
story: Race tests named a lock but passed with that lock removed, because a counter row serialized the work. The lesson was in every brief and followed in form. Nine of 11 gates took three rounds.
entry: A race test names a lock but passes with that lock removed. Both postings call open_document, which updates a per-type counter before any lock, so the counter serializes them. Rule: a race test proves a lock only if it fails with that lock removed. Method: remove one lock at a time.
steps: strains
The S04 slice held the root's brief, which already said to record a lock-removal experiment per race. The task is tests to write, not a problem. The session had compacted at least once.
breaks
Nothing fails. The race tests pass with or without their lock. A cheap model gets no signal and the ladder never starts. The root pushed the lesson into briefs outside the fetch path.
strains
Task words reach the S02 entry. For S08 the words share only 'race' and 'lock' with it.
breaks

Later failures share the claim, not the cause: counter row, a helper holding after deferred checks, a trigger lock, an earlier code variant, and no single lock load-bearing. One entry surfaces for all and is right for one.
not_specified
The design does not say which window gets the entry. The error was made by read-only Opus reviewers and the Fable root, not the slice. Whether a task-start entry survives compaction is not recorded.
breaks
The lesson was in every brief and followed in form. Experiments were run. They held after deferred checks, ran on an earlier variant, or removed the wrong layer.
strains
What decided was a reviewer reading, then model-run experiments, at least four later shown misleading. The store's re-check does not judge new race tests that a slice writes.
breaks
Opus reviewers noticed and handed up finding tables. Going up did not settle it. The Fable root's round-1 premise was wrong. It settled when locks were removed one at a time.
breaks
'Solved' moved twice. Round 1 said scope lock, round 2 counter, round 3 proved counter. A capture at the strong model's verdict stores the wrong lock.
breaks
Which lock decides depends on the whole lock set. Any added guard changes the answer without touching the test. Race footprints are identical in good and bad runs.

title: A reversal test leaves the database short
story: A migration reversal test migrated back and forward only to the old step. On the merged tree, 2 of 2570 tests failed in the same worker. The session had copied the template into two new tests.
entry: Clinic, Django, pytest-xdist. Full check on merged main fails 2 of 2570 with CheckViolation. A test migrates back to 0013 and forward only to 0014; once 0015 exists the worker's database stays at 0014. Fix: in the finally, migrate to the leaf nodes of the app.
steps: strains
The Opus session held its design, code and the earlier test it copied. The defect was unknown to everyone. A stored 'how to test a reversal' would be that same test.
breaks
No trigger. The session's full check passed 2570 and two Opus reviews found no P1. The failure appeared only on the merged tree, in another test order.
breaks
The error text named a business rule of the feature just built. A query in those words points at the real-data guard, not at a migration test in another file.
breaks
The nearest stored items are the earlier test, a latent defect, and a rows-left-behind fix. Same class, different mechanism. That fix does not cover schema state.
works
The failure arrived in the Fable root's main window as test output and stayed there through the fix. The root compacted about 100 s after writing the lesson down.
breaks
Reuse multiplied the defect. The session copied the template's finally into two new tests.
breaks
'Passes the full check' was not stable. 2570 passed on the branch, 2 of 2570 failed on the merged tree. The check that judges equality certified a wrong solution.
works
A red deterministic check, not a model, noticed it. The handoff was tool output. Fable fixed it in about a minute.
strains
The root wrote the rule into conventions within two minutes. Under the design's write rule, this one-attempt top-tier fix is routine and not recorded.
strains
The entry covers one reversal helper. A reversal written another way, or failing on another constraint, shares no words. The 12-worker prediction is untested.

title: Subagent writes: the probe overruled two Opus
source: Memory note 11-01; map-full.txt line 588; orchestration.md line 14; HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS line 23
story: A note said subagents cannot write report files. A Haiku probe wrote a one-line .txt and the root sided with it. Each rewrite widened or flipped the entry. Next day eight subagents were refused on report.md.
entry: Subagents launched with the Agent tool could not write their reports. Both Opus analysts said the harness blocks subagents from writing report files and returned the text. Sonnet extractors wrote files earlier, so it may depend on agent type or output size. Brief subagents to return the result.
steps: works
On 11 Nov the Fable root had 'subagents cannot write files' as an explicit question and had read the memory note.
works
The task was the question itself, so a lookup had a clear trigger.
works
'Subagent write file refused' matches the entry's words.
strains
The entry carried a paraphrase, not the tool error, and its own hedge pointed at the wrong variables. The deciding detail, 'report files', was only a phrase.
works
The entry sat in the root's main window and stayed there through the compile.
breaks
The session overrode a right entry with a weaker test: a Haiku agent writing a one-line .txt. It then called the rule an unchecked self-report. The probe tested a different condition.
breaks
The probe answered 'can a subagent write a file', not 'a report file'. The refusal text that decides it sat in 1 Nov transcripts, never read.
breaks
The ladder ran downward. A Haiku probe overruled two Opus observations and the Fable root sided with the probe. The original observers were right.
breaks
Each write widened or flipped the entry: 'report files', then 'file writes are refused', then 'They can'. Two contradictory entries, neither naming the condition.
breaks
On 12 Nov eight subagents hit the refusal on report.md. They adapted silently and the root never saw it. The saved compile keeps 'They can' and a remedy the refusal blocks.

title: A 'not found' that was a search gap
source: Critic check-wait-max; task.md files; root transcript 7f348b2c; verdicts.txt line 30
story: A critic searched task.md files and found no 34-minute wait, and called the owner's figure unsupported. The wait was printed in a root transcript the search never covered. A same-tier refuter with a wider search corrected it.
entry: Check-wait-max. The owner says check waits reach 34 minutes. Searched docs/tasks/*/task.md for 'waited' and '34 min'. Largest recorded waits: 742 s and 726 s. '34 minutes' not found. The owner's figure is not supported by the records.
steps: works
Each Opus map lane held the sweep cards and the critic's output. Its task was to classify the claim.
not_specified
The lanes did not decide to look anything up. The entry was pushed into their input. The design does not say whether a negative is pushed or fetched.
works
'34 minutes' and 'slot wait' hit the critic's entry exactly.
breaks
Exact match, wrong answer. The entry is a 'not found' whose scope excluded the root transcript where the check printed 'waited 2030 s'.
strains
One entry reached four parallel map lanes and the verdict writers at once, before anything checked it.
breaks
'Not in task.md' became 'in no file', then 'the owner's figure is wrong', then a stop rule. The person who was right was overruled by a stored negative.
breaks
Nothing checks a negative. Its footprint, the task.md files, stayed valid. Footprint validity cannot show that the search missed where the evidence lived.
strains
Caught by a same-tier Opus-high refuter with a refute-by-default brief and a wider search, not by a higher tier. The handoff carried the critic's search scope.
breaks
The correction reached two documents. One verdicts file still says 742 s. The 9 Nov observation was a measurement, never a solved problem, so no capture rule would have stored it.
strains
The refuter's side find entered the compile as a 'staggered resume list'. The 742 s copy survives in the evidence file a trial would run from.
